Most of the Sahrawi refugee population displaced by the conflict lives in camps near Tindouf, in southwestern Algeria, not inside Western Sahara itself
Fishing is one of the territory's main economic activities, employing a large share of the workforce along its Atlantic coastline
The territory's largest city, Laayoune, was founded by Spain in the 1930s around a natural water source
eh.currencyNote: No separate Western Saharan currency exists; the Moroccan dirham is used in Moroccan-administered areas, while the Algerian dinar and Mauritanian ouguiya circulate in the smaller Polisario-controlled areas and refugee camps

government.form: Unitary semi-presidential state under limited self-governance (Palestinian Authority administers parts of the West Bank; Gaza Strip governance has been disrupted by ongoing conflict); UN non-member observer state since 2012

ps.independence: 15 November 1988 (unilateral declaration of independence; recognized by a majority of UN member states but not by Israel, the US, and others; UN granted non-member observer state status in 2012)
ps.earliestSettlement: Jericho (Tell es-Sultan), continuously inhabited since roughly the 9th millennium BCE, among the oldest settlements on Earth

keyDates.event: Jericho and surrounding region settled by early Canaanite and biblical-era communities
Region comes under Islamic rule following the early Muslim conquests
Crusaders capture Jerusalem, establishing the Kingdom of Jerusalem
Ottoman Empire annexes the region, ruling it for four centuries
British Mandate for Palestine begins following World War I
UN General Assembly adopts Partition Plan (Resolution 181) proposing separate Jewish and Arab states
Establishment of Israel and the first Arab-Israeli war; large-scale Palestinian displacement (the Nakba)
Six-Day War; Israel occupies the West Bank and Gaza Strip
PLO unilaterally declares the State of Palestine
Oslo Accords establish the Palestinian Authority with limited self-rule
Israel withdraws settlers and troops from the Gaza Strip
Hamas takes control of governance in the Gaza Strip
UN General Assembly upgrades Palestine to non-member observer state status
Tell es-Sultan (ancient Jericho) inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site
War breaks out in Gaza following the 7 October attacks, triggering a prolonged and severe humanitarian crisis that continues to affect the territory

ps.climate: Mediterranean climate in the West Bank highlands and Gaza coast (hot, dry summers and mild, wet winters), transitioning to an arid desert climate in the Jordan Valley and around the Dead Sea, the lowest point on Earth's land surface

unesco.name: Church of the Nativity and the Pilgrimage Route, Bethlehem
Palestine: Land of Olives and Vines – Cultural Landscape of Southern Jerusalem, Battir

busiestAirport.name: No fully operational international airport; Yasser Arafat International Airport in Gaza has been closed/damaged since the early 2000s

funFacts: Jericho, in the West Bank, is considered one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities on Earth, with evidence of settlement dating back over 10,000 years.
Bethlehem, revered as the traditional birthplace of Jesus, draws Christian pilgrims from around the world, especially at Christmas.
The Dead Sea, bordering the West Bank, is the lowest point on Earth's land surface at roughly 430 meters below sea level and is so salty that swimmers float easily.
Olive trees cover a large share of Palestinian farmland, and olive oil production is central to both the economy and cultural identity.
Palestinian embroidery (tatreez), with patterns that vary by region and village, is a celebrated traditional art form recognized by UNESCO as part of humanity's intangible cultural heritage.
Poet Mahmoud Darwish is regarded as the Palestinian national poet, and his work is widely studied across the Arab world.
The city of Hebron is home to the Ibrahimi Mosque/Cave of the Patriarchs, a site sacred to Judaism, Christianity, and Islam alike.
Musakhan, roasted chicken on flatbread with sumac, onions, and pine nuts, is widely celebrated as the Palestinian national dish.
Nablus is famous for its traditional olive-oil soap industry and for knafeh, a popular sweet cheese pastry.
The Palestinian keffiyeh, a checkered scarf, has become one of the most recognizable cultural symbols associated with Palestinian identity.
ps.currencyNote: No separate Palestinian currency exists; the New Israeli Shekel is the primary currency in circulation, with the Jordanian Dinar also widely used in the West Bank and the US Dollar accepted in many transactions.

government.form: Unitary presidential republic (de facto independent; multi-party democracy with regular elections); recognized by Israel since December 2025 - the first UN member state to do so - though not by any other UN member state

somaliland.independence: 18 May 1991 (unilaterally redeclared independence from Somalia, reviving the sovereignty it briefly held after British withdrawal in 1960); recognized by Israel since December 2025, the first and only UN member state to do so
formerNames: State of Somaliland (1960, briefly independent before union with Somalia)
somaliland.earliestSettlement: Region inhabited since the Neolithic era; the rock art site of Laas Geel, dated to roughly 5,000 years ago, is among the earliest evidence of settled human activity

keyDates.event: Britain establishes the British Somaliland Protectorate through treaties with local clans
British Somaliland gains independence on 26 June and, days later, unites with the former Italian Somaliland to form the Somali Republic
Military coup brings Siad Barre to power over the Somali Republic
Somali National Movement (SNM) formed, leading an armed struggle against the Barre government
Civil war intensifies with heavy fighting and destruction in Hargeisa and other northern towns
Siad Barre's government collapses; Somaliland declares independence from Somalia on 18 May
Grand Conference of Borama establishes a clan-based power-sharing system and selects Muhammad Haji Ibrahim Egal as president
Constitutional referendum overwhelmingly approves Somaliland's constitution and independence
First multi-party presidential election held
Peaceful transfer of power through elections, cited internationally as a model of democratic stability in the region
Musa Bihi Abdi elected president in internationally observed elections
Abdirahman Mohamed Abdullahi (Irro) elected president in a peaceful transfer of power
Israel announces formal recognition of Somaliland, becoming the first UN member state to do so

somaliland.climate: Hot and arid to semi-arid across most of the territory, with a cooler, drier highland climate in the Golis Mountains and higher humidity along the Gulf of Aden coast

nationalDish.name: Bariis iyo Hilib Ari (rice with goat meat)

engineeringProjects: Berbera Port expansion and corridor (developed with DP World investment)
funFacts: Somaliland has run its own currency, passports, and elections since 1991, and was recognized by Israel in December 2025 - its first recognition from a UN member state.
The Laas Geel rock art complex near Hargeisa contains vividly preserved paintings of cattle and people estimated at roughly 5,000 years old.
Somaliland is frequently cited by regional observers as more stable and democratic than much of the rest of Somalia, with a series of peaceful transfers of power through elections.
The port city of Berbera has been a trading hub since antiquity, historically linked to incense routes to Arabia and the wider Red Sea world.
Camels remain central to Somaliland's economy and culture, and the country is among the world's leading exporters of live camels and other livestock, mainly to the Gulf states.
Hargeisa hosts an annual international book fair, one of the largest cultural events in the Horn of Africa.
Somaliland's flag features a black star over a white crescent and five-pointed star on a green, white, and red background, echoing the Somali Republic's pan-Somali flag colors.
Frankincense and myrrh, prized since ancient times, are still harvested from trees growing wild in Somaliland's highlands.
In December 2025, Israel became the first UN member state to formally recognize Somaliland as an independent state.
somaliland.currencyNote: The Somaliland shilling is not convertible internationally and circulates only within Somaliland; US dollars and mobile-money platforms (notably Zaad, run by Telesom) are widely used for everyday transactions.

government.form: Unitary presidential republic (partially recognized, de facto independent; recognized by Russia and a small number of UN member states; considered part of Georgia by the UN and most of the international community)
government.nationalDay: 30 September (Victory and Independence Day, marking the end of the 1992–93 war in Abkhazia)

abkhazia.independence: 1992–93 war in Abkhazia established de facto separation from Georgia; independence unilaterally declared via referendum in 1999; reinforced after the 2008 Russo-Georgian War when Russia formally recognized Abkhazia's independence (partial recognition: Russia, Nicaragua, Venezuela, Nauru, Syria)
formerNames: Abkhaz Autonomous Soviet Socialist Republic (1931–1991, within the Georgian SSR)
formerCapitals: Anacopia (778–786, capital of the medieval Kingdom of Abkhazia)
Kutaisi (786–1008, capital of the medieval Kingdom of Abkhazia)
abkhazia.earliestSettlement: The Black Sea coast was settled by ancient Colchian tribes from at least the 9th–6th centuries BC; Greek colonists founded the port of Dioscurias (on the site of modern Sukhumi) around the 6th century BC

keyDates.event: Greek colonists found the port city of Dioscurias on the site of modern-day Sukhumi
Leon II establishes the independent Kingdom of Abkhazia, with its capital at Anacopia
The Abkhazian royal capital is moved to Kutaisi
Bagrat III unites the Kingdom of Abkhazia with the Kingdom of the Iberians, forming a unified Kingdom of Georgia
Ottoman influence over the Abkhazian coast grows, gradually introducing Islam to the region
The Principality of Abkhazia becomes a protectorate of the Russian Empire
The Russian Empire abolishes the Abkhazian princedom and annexes the territory directly
The Abkhazian Soviet Socialist Republic is established
Abkhazia is downgraded to an Autonomous Soviet Socialist Republic within the Georgian SSR
War in Abkhazia breaks out between Georgian government forces and Abkhaz separatists, backed by North Caucasian and Cossack volunteers
Abkhaz forces take full control of Sukhumi, ending the war; most of the ethnic Georgian population flees or is expelled
Abkhazia holds an independence referendum and declares itself a sovereign state
Following the Russo-Georgian War, Russia formally recognizes Abkhazia's independence
Badra Gunba is elected President of Abkhazia

abkhazia.climate: Humid subtropical along the Black Sea coast, moderated by the Caucasus range; alpine and snowy in the mountainous interior
engineeringProjects: Inguri Dam and hydroelectric power station (one of the world's tallest concrete arch dams; the dam sits in Georgian-controlled territory while its power station and reservoir are in Abkhazia, and output is shared between both sides under a long-standing agreement)

busiestAirport.name: Sukhumi Babushara Airport (limited scheduled service; closed to regular civil aviation for most of the post-war period, with intermittent charter and Russian flights since 2023)

funFacts: Krubera Cave in Abkhazia's Arabika Massif is the world's deepest known cave, plunging over 2,197 metres below the surface.
Abkhazia's Black Sea coastline made it a major Soviet-era resort destination, with Sukhumi and Pitsunda once hosting millions of Soviet tourists annually.
Lake Ritsa, a turquoise alpine lake in the Caucasus foothills, was a favored retreat of Soviet leader Joseph Stalin, who had a dacha built on its shores.
The region's medieval Kingdom of Abkhazia (8th–10th centuries) predates the modern dispute with Georgia by over a thousand years.
Abkhazia is one of the few places on Earth where tea, citrus, and subtropical crops are grown at the same latitude as temperate Caucasus mountain peaks over 4,000 metres high.
New Athos Cave, one of the largest karst caves in the Caucasus, has an internal railway to carry tourists through its chambers.
The Abkhaz language belongs to the small Northwest Caucasian family and has one of the largest consonant inventories of any language in the world.
Abkhazia exports large quantities of tangerines and hazelnuts to Russia, its main trading partner, which accounts for the large majority of its foreign trade.
The 1992–93 war led to the flight or expulsion of most of Abkhazia's ethnic Georgian population, a demographic shift still disputed internationally.
Only four UN member states — Russia, Nicaragua, Venezuela, and Syria — formally recognize Abkhazia's independence; the rest of the world considers it part of Georgia.
abkhazia.currencyNote: The Russian ruble is the currency used in practice for all transactions; Abkhazia has issued its own commemorative 'apsar' coins, which are not in general circulation.

government.form: Unitary semi-presidential republic (partially recognized, de facto independent; recognized by Russia and a small number of UN member states; considered part of Georgia by the UN and most of the international community)
government.nationalDay: 20 September (Independence Day, marking the 1990 declaration of sovereignty from the Georgian SSR)

ossetia.independence: Sovereignty from the Georgian SSR declared 20 September 1990; full independence declared following the 1991–92 South Ossetia War; reinforced after the 2008 Russo-Georgian War when Russia formally recognized South Ossetia's independence (partial recognition: Russia, Nicaragua, Venezuela, Nauru, Syria)
formerNames: South Ossetian Autonomous Oblast (1922–1990, within the Georgian SSR)
Republic of South Ossetia–State of Alania (official name used since 2017, referencing the medieval Alania)
ossetia.earliestSettlement: The region has been inhabited since antiquity; the ancestors of modern Ossetians, the Alans, migrated into the central Caucasus foothills (including present-day South Ossetia) mainly after the Mongol destruction of the Alania kingdom in the 13th century

keyDates.event: The medieval kingdom of Alania, ancestral to the Ossetians, flourishes in the central Caucasus
Mongol invasions destroy the Alanian capital of Maghas, shattering Alania as a unified kingdom
Surviving Alan clans retreat into the Caucasus mountains, including the area of present-day South Ossetia, in the ethnogenesis of the modern Ossetians
The Russian Empire annexes the Kingdom of Kartli-Kakheti, bringing Georgian-ruled territory including South Ossetia under Russian control
Russian imperial authority is fully consolidated over South Ossetia
The South Ossetian Autonomous Oblast is established within the Georgian SSR
Georgian-Ossetian tensions escalate as Georgian nationalist movements grow during Soviet collapse
South Ossetia declares sovereignty from the Georgian SSR on 20 September
The South Ossetia War ends with a ceasefire, leaving South Ossetia de facto separated from Georgian control
The Russo-Georgian War breaks out over South Ossetia; Russia formally recognizes South Ossetia's independence afterward
South Ossetia formally adopts the name 'Republic of South Ossetia–State of Alania'
Alan Gagloev is elected President of South Ossetia
Gagloev resigns; Marat Kambolov becomes Acting President

ossetia.climate: Continental and alpine, strongly moderated by elevation; warmer, Mediterranean-influenced microclimates in the lower Liakhvi valley around Tskhinvali, with snowy conditions in the high Caucasus
engineeringProjects: Roki Tunnel (opened 1984, a 3.7 km Soviet-built road tunnel through the Greater Caucasus that is the only land route linking South Ossetia directly to Russia, and was the main logistics route for Russian forces during the 2008 war)

busiestAirport.name: No operating civilian airport; South Ossetia is reached overland via the Roki Tunnel from Russia or via Georgian-controlled roads

funFacts: South Ossetia's modern Ossetian population traces its ancestry to the Alans, an ancient Iranian-speaking people who once controlled Silk Road trade through the Caucasus.
The Roki Tunnel, South Ossetia's only direct land link to Russia, was bored through the Greater Caucasus in the early 1980s and remains its economic and military lifeline.
Mount Khalatsa, South Ossetia's highest point at 3,938 metres, sits in the rugged northern reaches of the territory along the main Caucasus range.
Ossetian is an Eastern Iranian language, making it a linguistic relative of Persian rather than of neighbouring Georgian or Russian.

The Ossetian pie, a round flatbread stuffed with cheese, meat, or herbs, is central to Ossetian hospitality and is traditionally served in groups of three at feasts, symbolizing the sun, sky, and earth.
Despite its small size, South Ossetia's terrain ranges from the warmer Liakhvi river valley around Tskhinvali to high alpine passes near the Russian border.
South Ossetia's state budget relies heavily on direct financial assistance from Russia, which has covered a large majority of its annual spending in recent years.
The region was officially renamed the 'Republic of South Ossetia–State of Alania' in 2017, explicitly invoking the medieval Alania kingdom as a historical ancestor.
ossetia.currencyNote: The Russian ruble is the only currency used in practice; South Ossetia has minted commemorative 'zarin' coins, which are not in general circulation.

government.form: Unrecognized unitary semi-presidential republic (self-administered breakaway territory on the east bank of the Dniester, internationally recognized as part of Moldova)

transnistria.independence: 2 September 1990 (unilaterally declared from the Moldavian SSR; fought a 1992 war with Moldova; a ceasefire has held since 21 July 1992; not recognized by any UN member state, and recognized only by the likewise-unrecognized states of Abkhazia and South Ossetia; Moldova and the broader international community consider it part of Moldova)
formerNames: Pridnestrovian Moldavian Soviet Socialist Republic (1990–1991 proclaimed name)
transnistria.earliestSettlement: The site of modern Tiraspol was long inhabited, with the ancient Greek colony of Tyras founded nearby on the Dniester around the 6th century BC; the present city was founded in 1792 by Russian general Alexander Suvorov as a fortress town

keyDates.event: Greek colonists found Tyras near the mouth of the Dniester
Russian general Alexander Suvorov founds the fortress of Tiraspol
The region becomes part of the Russian Empire's Bessarabia/Kherson governorates
The Moldavian Autonomous Soviet Socialist Republic is created on the left bank of the Dniester within Soviet Ukraine, with Tiraspol as its capital
The Moldavian SSR is formed, joining Bessarabia with part of the former autonomous republic
Transnistria unilaterally declares independence from the Moldavian SSR on 2 September
War of Transnistria fought between Transnistrian/Russian forces and Moldova (March–July)
Ceasefire agreement signed on 21 July, establishing a Russian-patrolled security zone that persists today
A local referendum (unrecognized internationally) overwhelmingly favors independence and eventual union with Russia
FC Sheriff Tiraspol, based in the territory, becomes the first Moldovan club to win a UEFA Champions League group-stage match, beating Real Madrid
Several unexplained explosions strike targets inside Transnistria following Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine, raising regional tension

transnistria.climate: Temperate continental climate with hot, relatively dry summers and cold winters, moderated somewhat by the Dniester river valley

busiestAirport.name: No functioning commercial airport; Tiraspol's small airport has no scheduled passenger service and travelers use Chișinău (Moldova) or Odesa (Ukraine)

funFacts: Transnistria still flies a flag featuring the Soviet hammer and sickle, one of the last places in the world to do so officially
Its de facto currency, the Transnistrian ruble, is issued in both paper and plastic (polymer) coin form, including unusual square and pentagonal-shaped denominations
Statues of Vladimir Lenin still stand in front of government buildings in Tiraspol
FC Sheriff Tiraspol stunned Real Madrid 2-1 in the 2021 UEFA Champions League, despite representing a territory recognized by no UN member state
The territory issues its own passports and license plates, which are not recognized outside Transnistria, Abkhazia, and South Ossetia
Transnistria has its own currency, flag, anthem, parliament, and army, functioning as a de facto state despite having no UN recognition
A large contingent of Russian troops has remained stationed in Transnistria since the 1992 ceasefire, officially as peacekeepers
Kvint, the state brandy distillery founded in the 19th century, exports cognac-style spirits that have won awards at international competitions
The territory is a narrow strip rarely more than about 20 km wide, squeezed between the Dniester River and the Ukrainian border
transnistria.currencyNote: The Transnistrian ruble is not convertible or recognized outside the territory and cannot legally be exported or imported; uniquely, Transnistria has issued coins made of pressed plastic rather than metal, including some non-circular (square and pentagonal) denominations.

government.form: Unrecognized unitary semi-presidential republic (self-administered northern third of the island of Cyprus, recognized as a sovereign state only by Turkey; the Republic of Cyprus and the broader international community consider the area under Turkish occupation)

ncyprus.independence: 15 November 1983 (unilaterally declared, following the 1974 division of Cyprus; recognized only by Turkey; the United Nations and the Republic of Cyprus regard the area as militarily occupied Cypriot territory)
ncyprus.earliestSettlement: Nicosia (Lefkoşa/Lefkosia), divided since 1974, traces settlement back over 2,500 years, with the walled city taking its present form under Lusignan and Venetian rule in the medieval period

keyDates.event: The Ottoman Empire conquers Cyprus from Venice
Britain assumes administration of Cyprus from the Ottoman Empire
Cyprus becomes a British Crown colony
Cyprus gains independence from Britain as a unitary republic with Greek and Turkish Cypriot communities
Intercommunal violence breaks out between Greek and Turkish Cypriots
A Greek-Cypriot-backed coup is followed by a Turkish military intervention on 20 July, dividing the island; the coastal resort of Varosha is abandoned and fenced off
The Turkish Federated State of Cyprus is proclaimed in the north
The Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus unilaterally declares independence on 15 November
Crossing points along the UN buffer zone open for the first time in decades, allowing movement between north and south

A UN reunification referendum (the Annan Plan) is approved by Turkish Cypriots but rejected by Greek Cypriots; the Republic of Cyprus joins the EU the same year, with application suspended in the north
Part of the fenced-off ghost town of Varosha is reopened to visitors for the first time since 1974

ncyprus.climate: Mediterranean climate with hot, dry summers and mild, wetter winters
funFacts: Northern Cyprus is recognized as a sovereign state only by Turkey; the rest of the world regards the area as part of the Republic of Cyprus under Turkish military control
Ercan International Airport has no direct international flights because of the long-standing embargo; all incoming flights must first touch down in mainland Turkey

Varosha, once a glamorous beach resort frequented by stars like Elizabeth Taylor and Brigitte Bardot, has stood largely abandoned behind fences since 1974, earning it the nickname 'ghost town'; parts reopened to visitors in 2020

Residents can hold TRNC passports, which have very limited international validity, but many Turkish Cypriots also hold Republic of Cyprus (and thus EU) passports, letting them travel and work freely across Europe
Hellim (halloumi) cheese is a point of dispute between the two communities after the Republic of Cyprus secured EU protected-status for 'Halloumi/Hellim' covering the whole island
Casino gambling, illegal in the Republic of Cyprus and mainland Turkey, is legal in Northern Cyprus, making it a hub for casino tourism
The UN Buffer Zone (Green Line) still runs through the middle of the capital, dividing North Nicosia (Lefkoşa) from Nicosia
Northern Cyprus uses the Turkish lira as its currency rather than the euro used in the Republic of Cyprus
St. Hilarion Castle and Bellapais Abbey, medieval Crusader-era landmarks in the Kyrenia mountains, are among the north's best-known historic sites
ncyprus.currencyNote: Northern Cyprus uses the Turkish lira, making it one of the few places where the local economy runs on a currency tied to high-inflation mainland monetary policy rather than its own or the euro used across the rest of the island.
